meaning: something that deviates from what is standard, normal or expected
sentence: A single warm week in December was dismissed as an anomaly until the same thing happened the next year.

meaning: a deep-seated feeling of dislike or aversion towards someone or something
sentence: Her antipathy to crowded markets kept her shopping at dawn.

meaning: to scold or criticise someone angrily and at length
sentence: The coach berated the fielders for a full ten minutes before anyone dared to speak.

meaning: to grow or increase rapidly; to begin to flourish
sentence: What began as a reading circle of four burgeoned into a library serving the whole village.

meaning: feeling genuine remorse for a wrong one has done
sentence: He returned the borrowed watch with a contrite note admitting that he had broken the strap.

meaning: to come together at a point; also, of opinions or paths, to grow steadily more alike
sentence: Three roads converge at the temple gate, which is why the traffic there never eases.

meaning: dejected and downcast after a disappointment
sentence: The crestfallen debater had already sat down when the judges announced that he had come first.

meaning: the way a person outwardly behaves and carries himself
sentence: His calm demeanour during the fire drill steadied the younger children more than any instruction could.

meaning: careful and tactful in what one says and does, so as to avoid offence or the revealing of private matters
sentence: A discreet cough from the doorway was enough to end the argument.

meaning: to make known information that was private or secret
sentence: The banker refused to divulge the account details even to the man's own brother.

meaning: a large and imposing building; also a complex system built up over a long time
sentence: The old courthouse is a grey edifice that dwarfs every shop on the street.

meaning: fair and impartial in the way it treats everyone concerned
sentence: The brothers agreed on an equitable division of the land rather than letting the eldest take the best fields.

meaning: to free someone or something from a difficulty or an entanglement
sentence: It took an hour to extricate the calf from the barbed wire without injuring it.

meaning: a mistaken belief, or a flaw in reasoning that makes an argument unsound
sentence: It is a common fallacy that the tallest player must be the best at the game.

meaning: conspicuously and outrageously bad, with no attempt at concealment
sentence: Parking across the ambulance bay was a flagrant disregard for everyone else in the hospital.

meaning: strikingly showy and confident in style or manner
sentence: His flamboyant orange turban could be picked out from the far end of the platform.

meaning: treating a serious matter with inappropriate lightness
sentence: A flippant answer to the examiner's question cost him more marks than silence would have.

meaning: to shock or stir someone into sudden and decisive action
sentence: The collapse of the footbridge galvanised the residents into petitioning the council at last.

meaning: closely relevant to the matter under discussion
sentence: Ask about the canteen budget later; it is not germane to a debate about the syllabus.

meaning: an excessive supply of something; also to fill or supply beyond what is needed
sentence: A glut of onions after the good monsoon pushed prices below what the farmers had spent on seed.

meaning: impressive in scale in a way that is absurdly pretentious
sentence: His grandiose plan for a marble stadium collapsed the moment someone asked who would pay for it.

meaning: cunning and deceit used to achieve one's ends
sentence: She got past the gatekeeper by guile rather than argument, claiming to be the electrician.

meaning: forbidden by law or by accepted custom
sentence: The forest guard traced the illicit felling to a contractor two districts away.

meaning: absolutely necessary and not to be put off; also a command that must be obeyed
sentence: It is imperative that the injured man reaches a hospital within the hour.

meaning: acting quickly and rashly, without thinking of the consequences
sentence: One impetuous jump from the moving train left him with a broken wrist and a long lecture.

meaning: done without preparation or rehearsal
sentence: An impromptu speech from the retiring teacher moved the hall far more than the printed programme did.

meaning: impossible to satisfy, however much is supplied
sentence: The child had an insatiable appetite for questions and wore out three uncles before lunch.

meaning: narrow-minded from having little contact with other people or ideas; also of or like an island
sentence: Two years in the same small office had made his opinions insular and hard to argue with.

meaning: fearless and resolute in the face of danger
sentence: An intrepid nurse crossed the flooded causeway twice a day to reach the marooned hamlet.

meaning: to flood with water; also to overwhelm with a great quantity of something
sentence: The office was inundated with applications within an hour of the notice appearing.

meaning: fond of joking, or said in a spirit of good humour
sentence: His jocular manner in the ward did more for the patients than the ward's radio ever did.

meaning: to place two things side by side so that the contrast between them stands out
sentence: The exhibition juxtaposes a village loom with a power loom to show what a century changed.

meaning: lacking energy or spirit; slow and pleasantly unhurried
sentence: The languid afternoon heat emptied the streets until well past four.

meaning: the treatment of a serious matter with humour or a lack of due respect
sentence: A little levity halfway through the long meeting kept everybody awake.

meaning: legal responsibility for something; also a person or thing that is a burden to others
sentence: A goalkeeper who cannot judge a high ball is a liability to the whole side.

meaning: to follow a winding course, or to wander about without any clear direction
sentence: The river meanders so widely across the plain that the road has to cross it four times.

meaning: of only ordinary or moderate quality, and so not good enough
sentence: A mediocre performance in the trial match cost him the captaincy he had been promised.

meaning: dull and ordinary; concerned with everyday matters rather than lofty ones
sentence: Between the ceremonies came the mundane duties: forms to sign, chairs to stack, lights to switch off.

meaning: extremely generous in giving
sentence: A munificent donation from a former pupil paid for the entire science block.

meaning: vague and ill-defined in form or in meaning
sentence: His plan for the business was nebulous: plenty of enthusiasm and not a single figure.

meaning: to make legally void, or to cancel out the effect of something
sentence: One careless foul nullified the advantage the team had spent an hour building.

meaning: not aware of what is happening around one
sentence: Oblivious to the queue behind him, he counted out the change coin by coin.

meaning: elaborately and heavily decorated
sentence: The ornate silver doors of the old palace take two men to swing open.

meaning: done or shown openly rather than being concealed
sentence: There was no overt quarrel between them, only a coldness that everyone noticed.

meaning: excessively concerned with small rules and formal details
sentence: His pedantic insistence on the exact form of the heading delayed the report by a week.

meaning: childishly sulky and bad-tempered over small things
sentence: A petulant refusal to shake hands after the match cost him the sportsmanship award.

meaning: evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret
sentence: The most poignant object in the museum is a child's slate, still carrying half a lesson.

meaning: an earlier action or decision taken as an example or a rule for later ones
sentence: Letting one class skip the drill would set a precedent that the whole school would claim.

meaning: to prevent something from happening or someone from doing something
sentence: A torn ligament precluded any thought of running the trials that season.

meaning: a right or privilege belonging to a particular person or office
sentence: Choosing the batting order is the captain's prerogative, not the crowd's.

meaning: a natural tendency to behave in a particular way
sentence: His propensity to argue with umpires kept him out of two finals.

meaning: outstanding skill or ability in a particular field
sentence: His prowess with a hockey stick was known in three districts before he turned sixteen.

meaning: a passing feeling of doubt or unease about one's own conduct
sentence: He signed the form without a qualm and regretted it within the week.

meaning: a peculiar habit or trait in a person's character; also a strange turn of events
sentence: By some quirk of the timetable, the two rival houses were given the same field every Friday.

meaning: bitter, long-lasting resentment left behind by a quarrel
sentence: The two families divided the orchard without rancour, which surprised the whole village.

meaning: a person who lives alone and avoids the company of others
sentence: The old painter became a recluse, leaving his gate locked and his letters unopened.

meaning: to restore friendly relations between people; also to make two accounts or ideas agree
sentence: It took a wedding to reconcile the brothers after eleven years of silence.

meaning: no longer needed or useful; also, of a worker, dismissed because the job has ceased to exist
sentence: The second paragraph is redundant, since it says exactly what the first one has already said.

meaning: a short period of rest or relief from something difficult
sentence: The evening breeze was the only respite from a day of unbroken heat.

meaning: to withdraw a statement as untrue; also to draw something back in
sentence: The newspaper retracted the story a week later, in four lines on page nine.

meaning: a trick or stratagem used to deceive someone
sentence: Sending the boy for water was a ruse to get him away from the gate.

meaning: severely and wittily critical
sentence: The editor's scathing review of the play had emptied the theatre by the third night.

meaning: dark and gloomy in colour or in mood; grave in manner
sentence: The team returned in sombre silence, the trophy left behind for another year.

meaning: to reject something or someone with contempt
sentence: He spurned the offer of a settlement and insisted on hearing the verdict.

meaning: extremely dirty and wretched, especially from neglect or poverty
sentence: Three families shared a squalid room behind the timber yard with one tap between them.

meaning: sedate, respectable and unadventurous
sentence: The staid old bank would not lend a rupee to anybody under thirty.

meaning: very loyal and committed in attitude; also to stop the flow of blood from a wound
sentence: He remained a staunch supporter of the club through fifteen losing seasons.

meaning: a mark of disgrace attached to a person or a circumstance
sentence: The stigma of having failed once kept him from applying again for three years.

meaning: easily influenced or harmed by a particular thing
sentence: Seedlings raised indoors are susceptible to the first cold night outside.

meaning: equivalent in effect to something, usually to something bad
sentence: Refusing to answer the auditor's question was tantamount to admitting that the money had gone.

meaning: done as a trial and not yet settled; also hesitant and unsure
sentence: They pencilled in a tentative date for the match, subject to the ground drying out.

meaning: very weak or slight, and so unlikely to hold
sentence: The link between the two thefts was tenuous, resting on a single similar footprint.

meaning: a long and angry speech of criticism or accusation
sentence: A ten-minute tirade about the state of the changing room greeted the players at half-time.

meaning: a feeling of fear or nervousness about something that is about to happen
sentence: She opened the results envelope with real trepidation, having missed a month of school.

meaning: present or found everywhere
sentence: Plastic sachets are now ubiquitous, turning up in riverbeds a hundred kilometres from the nearest shop.

meaning: strange in an unsettling way; also strikingly accurate beyond ordinary explanation
sentence: She has an uncanny memory for faces and can still name a boy she taught twenty years ago.

meaning: done by one side only, without the agreement of the others concerned
sentence: A unilateral change to the timetable annoyed every department that had not been consulted.

meaning: to seize a position or power wrongfully and by force
sentence: The general usurped the throne while the young king was still in exile.

meaning: conformity to the truth; habitual truthfulness
sentence: The court had no reason to doubt the veracity of a witness with nothing to gain.

meaning: able to adapt to many different functions or activities
sentence: A versatile all-rounder is worth two specialists on a tour with a thin squad.

meaning: to speak or write about someone in an abusive and belittling way
sentence: He was vilified in the local press for a decision the whole committee had taken together.

meaning: to refrain from insisting on a right, a fee or a rule
sentence: The hospital waived its fee once it learned that the family had lost everything in the flood.

meaning: to decrease gradually in size, strength or importance
sentence: Interest in the evening classes waned as soon as the harvest began.

meaning: self-willed and difficult to control, following one's own unpredictable course
sentence: A wayward younger brother kept the whole household anxious for a decade.

meaning: full of a gentle, yearning regret for something past or unattainable
sentence: He gave a wistful look at the cricket field as the bus pulled out for the last time.

meaning: the direct opposite of something; or a contrast of two ideas placed deliberately side by side
sentence: His quiet, careful manner was the antithesis of his brother's noisy confidence.

meaning: to charm or delight someone; or to win a person over by charm in order to deceive them
sentence: The salesman beguiled the old couple into signing a contract they never once read.

meaning: the rise and fall of the voice in speech; or a regular rhythm of sound or movement
sentence: You could recognise the old announcer by the slow cadence of his voice alone.

meaning: the use of threats or force to make a person act against their will
sentence: The confession was thrown out because it had plainly been made under duress.

meaning: insolent and shameless boldness in behaviour
sentence: He had the effrontery to ask for a raise the week after losing the account.

meaning: the point at which a plan or long effort finally bears results
sentence: The village library came to fruition after nine years of fundraising by one teacher.

meaning: to bring oneself into someone's favour by flattery or deliberate effort to please
sentence: He tried to ingratiate himself with the new principal by praising every decision she made.

meaning: a long and tedious recital of complaints or events; or a series of prayers with set responses
sentence: The meeting opened, as always, with a litany of complaints about the canteen.

meaning: a loose sleeveless cloak; or a role or responsibility passed from one person to the next
sentence: She took up the mantle of her father's long campaign for cleaner rivers.

meaning: the responsibility or duty of doing a particular thing
sentence: The onus is on the seller to prove that the goods were genuine.

meaning: all the generations of people who will come after the present one
sentence: He kept every letter so that posterity might understand what the famine had been like.

meaning: the combining of separate parts or ideas into a single connected whole
sentence: Her essay was a careful synthesis of three arguments nobody had thought to read together.

meaning: the curved path of a moving object; or the course something takes as it develops over time
sentence: The trajectory of his career changed the day he was posted to the frontier.

meaning: a violent or sudden change that disturbs a settled state of affairs
sentence: Partition brought an upheaval that emptied whole streets in a single week.

meaning: an event marking a turning point after which things are different; or a ridge dividing two river systems
sentence: The war of nineteen seventy-one proved a watershed in the region's history.
